date_note: GBHackers says the advisory was issued on 18 November; the GBHackers article was published 23 November. The advisory itself was not read.
title: India's I4C warns that unauthorised access to a signed-in WhatsApp Web session can expose messages
summary: GBHackers reports that the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, part of India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, issued an advisory on 18 November. It warns that unauthorised access to a signed-in WhatsApp Web session can expose private messages. GBHackers notes the advisory names no particular exploit and does not indicate a breach of WhatsApp's infrastructure.
plain: GBHackers reports an Indian government advisory warning that someone who gets into a signed-in WhatsApp Web session can read private messages. It names no specific exploit.
exec: An Indian agency warns, per GBHackers, that shared or public computers left signed in to WhatsApp Web expose messages.
action: I4C advises, per GBHackers, logging out manually after each WhatsApp Web session and avoiding cybercafes, public kiosks and borrowed computers.

validation.note: Only GBHackers read; the I4C advisory itself (i4c.mha.gov.in) was not read.
